Typically, multiple convolutions are applied to the input x and stored in channels. a) A convolution is applied to create hidden units h; to he, which form the first channel. b) A second convolution operation is applied to create hidden units hr7 to hi2, which form the second channel. The channels are stored in a 2D array H; that contains all the hidden units in the first hidden layer. c) If we add a further convolutional layer, there are now two channels at each input position. Here, the 1D convolution defines a weighted sum over both input channels at the three closest positions to create each new output channel.
